note: Analyst verdicts for the 6 REQUIRES-LOCALITY recordings from RESULTS.md, after the Stage-1 catalogue join. Evidence grades: the web tracks are published-guide tracks; the FZ_AMPHIBIA catalogue is the Fonoteca's OWN collection, so its envelope is institutional-usage evidence, not the track's own metadata. Guide scope is bibliographic (the /sonidos track sequences are the Fonoteca's published sound guides). Verdicts that rest on guide scope + envelope are labelled as such and are one step weaker than a per-recording locality record, which does not exist for these tracks.

evidence: Catalogue envelope for the filed name: 3/3 own-collection records are Balearic (Mallorca: Cap Blanc; Islas Baleares), recordist Rafael Marquez (the guide's author).
Balearic green-toad populations are Bufotes balearicus, not B. viridis s.s. (Dufresnes et al. 2019 partition of the viridis complex); B. viridis s.s. does not occur in the Balearics.
The web tracks sit in the Spain & Portugal guide's track sequence, whose green-toad material is the Balearic/Iberian material.
Catalogue envelope: 118/118 own-collection records are Iberian (ES 56: Salamanca, Avila; PT 62: Portalegre, Coimbra), recordist Rafael Marquez.
All four provinces lie inside Hyla molleri's range and outside the NE-Iberian zone where H. arborea s.s. enters the peninsula (Stoeck et al. 2008 partition).
The web track is the Spain & Portugal guide's tree-frog track.
No catalogue envelope exists (0 records under the filed name) - resolution rests on guide scope alone.

The track is the paired 'mini' track beside track 4 'Bufo Granulosus Major' in the Bolivia guide; Narvaes & Rodrigues (2009) restricted Rhinella granulosa s.s. to NE Brazil and the Bolivian member of the complex is R. major - the same species track 4 was elevated to in RESULTS.md.
resolutions.strength: moderate (guide scope + revision geography; no locality record)
